raw:
{
  "need": "Identity",
  "secondary": { "name": "Autonomy" },
  "read": "Your kid is not attacking your faith — they are doing the hard developmental work of figuring out what they actually believe versus what they inherited. The dinner-table announcement is a flag planted in public: it is a bid to be taken seriously as someone whose inner life matters, not just corrected back into compliance. The autonomy piece shows up in the dramatic declaration — they chose the most visible moment possible because they needed to feel like their decision had real weight.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Lay down the law — this is our family, these are our values, you are going as long as you live under this roof — which turns a faith question into a power contest and almost guarantees they dig in and associate church with control forever." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the expectation that they engage with their faith seriously and honestly, while opening up real conversation about what they are wrestling with — so they experience you as someone safe enough to actually think this through with, not someone they have to defeat.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "Taking your beliefs seriously and being willing to examine them honestly is not optional — that is what people of real conviction do.",
    "Checking out entirely without any reflection is not the standard in this family; whatever you land on, it has to be thought through."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "How they engage — attending a different service, reading, having conversations with you or a trusted adult, taking a short intentional break with a defined check-in — all of that is negotiable.",
    "The timeline and the form participation takes can flex; the expectation that they wrestle with it honestly rather than just walk away does not."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I heard what you said at dinner and I am not going to pretend it did not land hard for me, because it did. But I also know you do not say things like that out of nowhere, and I want to actually understand what is going on with you, not just react." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "So tell me what is underneath this. Is it something specific that happened, something you have been thinking about for a while, questions you have that feel unanswered? I am asking because I genuinely want to know what you are sitting with, not so I can argue you out of it." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is where I am coming from: I am not going to pretend faith is just a preference like what you want for dinner. It matters deeply to me and to this family, and I think you deserve to figure out what you actually believe — not just reject it to reject it and not just accept it because I said so. I think you are someone who can handle the real questions, and I want to help you find a way to do that seriously." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding you to this: you do not get to just tap out on something this important without really sitting with it. That is the standard I have for you because I think you are more than capable of that kind of honesty with yourself. Let us figure out together what that looks like for the next few months — that part I am genuinely open on." }
  ],
  "longGame": "How you handle this moment will determine whether you are someone they can bring the real questions to for the next thirty years or someone they have to hide their doubts from. Stay curious longer than feels comfortable, and they are far more likely to stay connected to both the faith and to you."
}
situation: My kid announced at dinner they are done with church and are not going anymore.
